claims.text: Variations in solute diffusion kinetics control the extent of dynamic strain aging across single-phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Dynamic strain aging governs differences in yield strength, ductility, and strain-rate sensitivity among these alloys.
Constituent cost and abundance modulate solute diffusion kinetics.
The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline can exist as a single-phase FCC alloy.
The proposed quaternary and ternary derivatives are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Tensile testing from 10^(-4) to 10^(-1) s^(-1), from room temperature to about 200 degrees Celsius, can be used as the controlled mechanical investigation.
Tracer or isotope diffusion experiments will determine activation energies for solute diffusion under matched processing histories.
Serrated flow combined with diffusion activation energies can establish a correlation between intermittent dislocation pinning and dynamic strain aging.
Changing the alloying constituents changes activation-energy barriers associated with diffusion.
Replacing higher-cost elements with cheaper, more diffusive elements lowers solute-migration activation energies.
Lower solute-diffusion activation energies promote dynamic strain aging.
Dynamic strain aging causes intermittent dislocation pinning and jerky flow.
Intermittent dislocation pinning associated with dynamic strain aging enhances yield strength.
Dynamic strain aging influences ductility through changes in strain-rate sensitivity.
Alloys having lower measured diffusion activation energies should show more pronounced serrated flow than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Alloys having lower measured diffusion activation energies should show heightened strain-rate sensitivity relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Grain boundaries or secondary phases can dominate the mechanical response and thereby limit application of the proposed diffusion-controlled mechanism.
Prior evidence demonstrates dynamic strain aging in similar high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis would be falsified if diffusion activation energies fail to correlate with the onset or intensity of serrated flow and strain-rate sensitivity relative to the baseline.
